sections.html:
Warren County is a south central Iowa county in the Des Moines metropolitan area, with Indianola as its county seat. It covers 573 square miles, of which 570 are land.

Polk County lies to the north, Marion to the east, Lucas to the southeast, Clarke to the southwest and Madison to the west. The county was formed in 1846 and named for General Joseph Warren of the American Revolution.

The Des Moines end of the county is urban, and the south is farmland. About 52.9 percent of residents live in urban areas and 47.1 percent in rural areas.

sections.h2: How many people live in Warren County, and where?
sections.html:
Warren County had 52,403 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 57,331 in 2025. Growth from 2010 to 2020 was 13.4 percent, and the median age is 38.8.

sections.h2: What is Indianola like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Indianola is a college and balloon town about 19 miles south of downtown Des Moines. It was founded in 1849 near the geographic center of the county and incorporated in 1863.

Simpson College, a United Methodist liberal arts school, was founded in Indianola in 1860. The National Balloon Classic runs for nine days each summer, and the National Balloon Museum is in town. The city has a municipal gigabit-capable fiber network.

Iowa Highway 92 crosses the city and meets US 65 and 69 southeast of downtown. Des Moines International Airport is about 13 miles northwest. The Indianola Community School District runs four elementary schools, a middle school and a high school.

Indianola requires rental owners to register and have rentals inspected every two years, with 24 hours notice to tenants before an inspection. A seller with a rented house should confirm its certificate with Code Enforcement at 515-962-5275.

sections.h2: Why did Norwalk and Carlisle grow so quickly?
sections.html:
Norwalk grew because annexations and new subdivisions brought houses to the edge of the Des Moines metro. Its population went from 6,884 in 2000 to 8,945 in 2010, 12,799 in 2020 and an estimated 15,004 in 2025.

Michael Foods is building an $85 million distribution center and is described as the largest single-site taxpayer in Warren County. Norwalk sits just south of Des Moines International Airport. A rainfall event in 2011 dropped more than 9 inches in 24 hours, and an EF4 tornado struck on March 5, 2022.

Carlisle lies between the North and Middle rivers near where they meet the Des Moines River. The town was founded in 1851 and incorporated in May 1870. It had 3,497 residents in 2000 and 4,160 in 2020, and its school district has campuses in Carlisle and Hartford.

sections.h2: What do Warren County courthouse offices handle?
sections.html:
The county's main offices are in the Administration Building at 301 N. Buxton Street in Indianola. The 1939 courthouse was condemned in late 2018, and the Warren County Justice Center opened in summer 2022.

  • Treasurer: Suite 102, 515-690-9240, propertytax@warrencountyia.org. Hours are 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. The page says service is by appointment, so call ahead.
  • Assessor: Suite 108, 515-690-9170, assessor@warrencountyia.org, listed under Janet Bunce.
  • Recorder: Suite 109, 515-690-9110, recorder@warrencountyia.org. The page also links the Declaration of Value form and a transfer tax calculator.

Property tax can be paid online through iowatreasurers.org, where Warren County is listed as county ID 91.

sections.h2: How does the Warren County Assessor set value?
sections.html:
The Warren County Assessor sets value at 100 percent of fair market value as of January 1, before any state rollback factor is applied. Real property is revalued every two years.

  • An informal review with the assessor is open April 2 through April 25.
  • A written Board of Review protest is open April 2 through April 30, limited to the grounds in Iowa Code 441.37.
  • In odd-numbered equalization years, notices are due by October 8. Protests of equalization changes are taken October 9 through October 31, and the Board sits October 10 through November 15.

The assessor does not collect tax or set rates. Those jobs belong to the treasurer and to the taxing bodies that set levies after public hearings. The county site links forms for the homestead credit, military exemption, disabled veteran credit and family farm.

sections.h2: What does a Warren County tax bill look like in fiscal 2027?
sections.html:
Warren County's fiscal 2027 county levy is 5.64659 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property and 8.38166 for rural property. Those figures are down 3.36 and 2.80 percent from fiscal 2026.

The residential rollback, which turns assessed value into taxable value, is 44.5345 percent for fiscal 2027 against 47.4316 percent the year before. Residential property makes up 87 percent of assessed value and 80 percent of taxable value in the county.

sections.h2: When are Warren County property taxes due, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Iowa property tax is paid in two halves. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, and late interest of 1.5 percent is added on the first of each month after the grace date.

In an ordinary sale, taxes are prorated and the buyer is credited with the seller's share, which the settlement statement should show. Unpaid city utility or service charges can also be certified to the county treasurer and collected like taxes, so a title company will look for them.

Transfers carry Iowa's real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500, owed by the seller under Iowa Code 428A.3. The recorder will not record a taxable deed until it is paid.

sections.h2: What happens at the Warren County tax sale?
sections.html:
Warren County sold its 2026 delinquent parcels online on Monday, June 15, 2026, starting at 8:30 a.m. through the GovEase platform. The delinquent list was published in the June 1 edition of The Carlisle Citizen.

  • Owners are notified within 15 days of the sale.
  • Redemption costs the sale amount plus 2 percent a month, with each part of a month counted as a whole month.
  • A 90-day redemption notice can be issued after 1 year and 9 months for a regular sale, or after 9 months for a public bidder sale.
  • Fees include $20 for a certificate and $25 for a treasurer's deed.

An owner behind on taxes can still sell, and the balance is paid from the proceeds. A parcel already sold at tax sale needs a redemption payment first.

sections.h2: How do we help Warren County owners with tax trouble?
sections.html:
We buy Warren County houses as-is, including houses with delinquent taxes, a tax sale certificate or an unpaid utility lien. We ask for the address and the tax statement, then reply with a written offer.

A written offer is a number you can compare to the redemption amount and to your own plans. You can turn it down and owe nothing.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Warren County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Indianola is the county seat. It had 15,833 residents in 2020, and the county administration offices are at 301 N. Buxton Street.

faqs.q: How do I protest a Warren County assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the assessor for an informal review between April 2 and April 25, or file a written Board of Review protest between April 2 and April 30. The Board's protest grounds are listed in Iowa Code 441.37.

faqs.q: Which Warren County school district has the highest levy?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2027, Carlisle has the highest school levy at 17.22926 per $1,000, followed by Indianola at 17.11308. Pleasantville is lowest at 14.19761.

faqs.q: How is the residential rollback changing in Warren County?
faqs.a: The county's fiscal 2027 residential rollback is 44.5345 percent, down from 47.4316 percent in fiscal 2026. A lower rollback reduces the share of assessed value that is taxed.

faqs.q: What does it cost to redeem a Warren County tax sale parcel?
faqs.a: The owner pays the sale amount plus 2 percent per month, counting any part of a month as a full month, plus a certificate fee of $20. Call the treasurer at 515-690-9240 for an exact payoff.
